title: Social role participation and inflammation: A meta-analytic examination of the shape of association and variability with age
title_zh: 社会角色参与与炎症：关于关联形态与年龄变异的荟萃分析
abstract: Social role participation is theorized to relate to physical health through systemic inflammation. We conducted a meta-analysis quantifying the association between social role participation and systemic inflammatory markers. Specifically, we synthesized studies assessing social integration (the degree of participation in a variety of social relationships) and social isolation (having few to no social ties), two indicators of social role participation. We further evaluated whether the association between social participation and inflammation followed graded or threshold patterns and whether its magnitude varied across adult development. A systematic search identified 50 articles, contributing 77 effect sizes. Meta-analyses were conducted using random effects models with robust variance estimation and controlled for study quality and effect size conversion confidence. Results indicated that greater social role participation was associated with lower inflammation (age-unadjusted r = -.054, p < .001; age-adjusted r = -.037, p < .001). Moreover, we found evidence for a graded pattern, such that compared to the most isolated group, increasingly integrated groups showed progressively stronger inverse effect sizes with inflammation (b = -.04, p = .017). We found weak evidence that the magnitude of the social role participation-inflammation link was moderated by age. In a subset of the analyses, this link was stronger for older (vs. younger) samples. However, this only emerged in the model that also adjusted for other study characteristics (e.g., inflammatory marker, study design). This review is the first to synthesize evidence across social integration and isolation, showing that greater social role participation is associated with progressively lower levels of inflammation.
abstract_zh: 社会角色参与被认为通过系统性炎症与身体健康相关。我们进行了一项荟萃分析，量化社会角色参与与系统性炎症标志物之间的关联。具体而言，我们综合了评估社会整合（在多种社会关系中参与程度）和社会孤立（几乎没有社会联系）的研究，这两者是社会角色参与的指标。我们进一步评估了社会参与与炎症之间的关联是否呈梯度或阈值模式，以及其幅度是否随成人发展而变化。系统检索识别出50篇文章，贡献了77个效应量。荟萃分析采用随机效应模型与稳健方差估计，并控制了研究质量和效应量转换置信度。结果显示，较高的社会角色参与与较低的炎症相关（未调整年龄时 r = -.054, p < .001；调整年龄后 r = -.037, p < .001）。此外，我们发现了梯度模式的证据，即与最孤立组相比，整合程度越高的群体在炎症方面呈现越强的负向效应（b = -.04, p = .017）。我们对社会角色参与-炎症关联幅度是否受年龄调节的证据较弱。在部分分析中，该关联在老年样本中更强，但仅在同时调整其他研究特征（如炎症标志物、研究设计）的模型中出现。该综述首次综合了社会整合与孤立的证据，表明更高的社会角色参与与逐步降低的炎症水平相关。
